findings.title: Wire the new timeout setting into the shutdown drain
findings.problem: GeneralConfig(shutdown_drain_timeout=120.5) accepts and preserves the value, but shutdown still uses _SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT, initialized solely from the environment or 60.0 in triggarr/search/scheduler.py:58–81 and passed to asyncio.timeout at line 634. Thus an operator configuring a longer drain still gets forced resource closure after 60 seconds. No runtime consumer reads the new field.

findings.fix_hint: Use the active general.shutdown_drain_timeout as the shutdown default, preserving the environment override, and add an integration test proving a non-default configuration reaches the drain timeout.
source_window: # Defense in depth: a TOML inf cannot unbound the drain. Config value is the default;
# TRIGGARR_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT env overrides at shutdown; form clamp (3600.0) is the UI ceiling.
shutdown_drain_timeout: float = Field(default=60.0, ge=1.0, allow_inf_nan=False)
# v2.2: skip Radarr movies without past digital/physical release date
skip_unreleased: bool = True

members.title: shutdown_drain_timeout config field is not read anywhere, so setting it has no effect
members.problem: The new field's comment says the config value is the default and that TRIGGARR_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT overrides it at shutdown. But triggarr/search/scheduler.py:58-81 still reads only the env var, once, at import time (`_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT = _read_shutdown_drain_timeout()`). The drain sites at scheduler.py:611-656 use that module constant and never look at settings.general.shutdown_drain_timeout. Right now a user who sets the field in TOML (or in the UI later) sees it accepted but ignored. The repo is in the middle of a TDD phase (commit 9bfd4a6), so the wiring may land in a later plan step. pending: confirm the scheduler refactor that reads this field is part of the same change set before release.

members.why_it_matters: A persisted setting that is silently ignored makes operators believe the drain is configured when it is not.
members.fix_hint: refactor _read_shutdown_drain_timeout to take settings.general.shutdown_drain_timeout as its default and call it at shutdown instead of at import

members.title: No upper bound on the model; the 3600s ceiling is enforced only by the form clamp
members.problem: The comment calls the form clamp (3600.0) the UI ceiling, but the model only has ge=1.0. A TOML-edited value such as 1e9 passes validation. It would hold shutdown well past the docker stop_grace_period of 90s, so SIGKILL would end the drain instead of the timeout (docker-compose.yml:24 and README.md:86 say the grace period must exceed the drain timeout). allow_inf_nan blocks inf but not very large finite values. The sibling field max_consecutive_failures sets both ge and le. pending: confirm whether a model-level le (for example le=3600.0) is intended to match the form clamp.
